summary: Source-anchored research for transformIdentifiers HMAC privacy mode. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: MongoDB's query stats README labels the subtype-8 hmacKey as sensitive data, and NIST describes HMAC as used with a shared secret key. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/query_stats/README.md ; https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/198-1/final

MongoDB's tokenization preserves relationships among repeated identifiers: the README says it lets MongoDB detect when two queries use the same identifiers, but never reveal what those identifiers were. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/query_stats/README.md

transformIdentifiers does not anonymize every $queryStats output field. MongoDB leaves MQL operators, aggregation parameter names, and client metadata such as application, driver, and operating-system details readable; it normalizes field values to their types instead of HMACing them, and says it does not store user field values. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

MongoDB Jira records why the project chose transform terminology: HMAC creates a tokenized identifier rather than deleting it as redaction would imply. The follow-up parameter change records the nested transformIdentifiers document with algorithm and hmacKey, replacing the earlier applyHmacToIdentifiers name. (high confidence) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-76424 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-77179

The optional $queryStats transformIdentifiers document currently requires algorithm hmac-sha-256 and a subtype-8 BinData hmacKey. MongoDB applies HMAC-SHA-256 to document field names, collection names, and database names. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

MongoDB's README says the transform applies HMAC-SHA-256 to the names of any field, collection, or database, and the Application Name field is not transformed. It calls the result a one-way tokenized object, which lets MongoDB detect when two queries use the same identifiers without revealing what those identifiers were. Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/query_stats/README.md

For transformed reads, current MongoDB documentation requires both queryStatsRead and queryStatsReadTransformed; the built-in clusterMonitor role includes both. A MongoDB design ticket explains that the project intended separate authorization for transformed and non-tokenized reads. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querystats/ ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-79071

MongoDB Atlas documentation says Atlas periodically runs $queryStats for product analytics and uses a unique HMAC key per Atlas organization; it states that collected query-stat data is retained for four years. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)
